title.en: Proof-Carrying Experimental Science: Interpretive Bridge Between AIFC, JANUS Proof-of-Observation, and Janus-Fundamentum
title.ru: Proof-Carrying Experimental Science: интерпретационный мост между AIFC, JANUS Proof-of-Observation и Janus-Fundamentum

purpose: Explain for future researchers, reviewers, replicators and AI collaborators the methodological insight that becomes visible when AIFC, JANUS Proof-of-Observation and Janus-Fundamentum are read together: the strongest common object is not a prediction machine or a single domain theory, but a research architecture in which a scientific claim must carry auditable evidence, provenance, replay obligations, adversarial tests, explicit failure states and a machine-readable ceiling on what may be concluded.

dialogue_origin.context: A research discussion asked what the existing AIFC and JANUS records imply at a higher methodological level, and why the research profile 'Independent researcher developing proof-carrying, adversarial scientific protocols' is more than descriptive branding.
dialogue_origin.researcher_realization: AIFC is better understood not as a machine for predicting future random events, but as an attempt to define the complete evidence standard required before a claim that information existed before an independently generated future random object is scientifically admissible.
dialogue_origin.interpretive_step: The same pattern was recognized in JANUS Proof-of-Observation and Janus-Fundamentum: each system tries to make a claim inseparable from the evidence required to audit, replay, attack and potentially reject it.
dialogue_origin.boundary: The dialogue records the emergence of an interpretation. It does not establish global novelty of the phrase, a new scientific field, or community acceptance.

core_realization.better_compression: AIFC defines what must be proven before a claim that information existed before an independently generated future random object may be graded as incompatible with a declared forward-causal null.
core_realization.generalized_compression: A research claim should not arrive as prose alone. It should arrive with a machine-auditable evidence package that defines provenance, admissible side information, verifier logic, attack surface, failure conditions, replay obligations, selection rules and the strongest conclusion that may be promoted if all gates pass.
core_realization.epistemic_target: Make claims about causality, computation and observation checkable rather than merely persuasive.
core_realization.anti_self_deception_target: Construct the research process so that attractive false victories are structurally harder to promote than honest OPEN, BLOCKED, NULL or NEGATIVE outcomes.

janus_fundamentum.question: What must accompany a mathematical or computational claim so that a surviving result is not confused with proof?
characteristic_rules: CORPUS RESULT WITHOUT INDEPENDENT REPLAY = NON_FUNDAMENTUM
PUBLIC CLAIM WITHOUT REACHABLE PROVENANCE = OPEN, NOT TRUTH
VERIFIER CONTROLLED BY THE CLAIMANT = INDEPENDENCE NOT ESTABLISHED
janus_fundamentum.main_contribution_to_bridge: A claim is a state in a proof process, not a sentence. Candidate, executable, admitted, blocked and terminal states are intentionally non-equivalent.

janus_proof_of_observation.role: Proof-carrying experimental observation discipline for live computational systems.
janus_proof_of_observation.question: How can one prove that a computational exposure or state transition actually occurred under frozen semantics without overclaiming what that observation implies about outcome quality?
janus_proof_of_observation.main_contribution_to_bridge: Separate exposure integrity from outcome claims. A reproducibly segmented cohort can be an admitted engineering observation while SHA-256 weakness, better mining odds, energy savings or altered output distribution remain unproved.
janus_proof_of_observation.compressed_principle: Prove what the experiment did before arguing about what the result means.

aifc.role: Proof-carrying causal and temporal evidence discipline.
aifc.question: What evidence stack is required before a claim that pre-existing bytes contained information about a later independently generated random target may be graded as incompatible with a specified forward-causal null?
aifc.main_contribution_to_bridge: Move causal claims from narrative time-ordering to explicit adversarially audited premises covering freeze-time side information, target freshness, multiplicity, d-separation, sequential validity, rollback resistance and Byzantine witness continuity.
aifc.compressed_principle: Do not ask whether the result feels impossible under ordinary causality; define the ordinary causal null precisely enough that the incompatibility claim can fail closed.

proof_carrying_claim_model.informal_model: claim -> paper/log -> trust that procedure, chronology and analysis were as described
proof_carrying_claim_model.proof_carrying_model: claim + frozen inputs + provenance + evidence + verifier + replay + adversarial tests + negative-result retention + explicit failure classes + claim ceiling -> admissible status
minimum_claim_packet: claim identifier and exact semantic scope
proof_carrying_claim_model.key_property: Evidence is not an appendix added after the claim. The evidence contract is part of the claim's semantics.

aifc_as_experimental_wing_of_fundamentum.interpretation: Fundamentum defines an epistemic discipline for proof-search; AIFC extends the same discipline into experiments where time, randomness, causality, side information and external witnesses must themselves become auditable proof obligations.

mapping.witness_ledger: PRE_RETURN certificate + target-generation receipt + full evidence stack
mapping.independent_replay: independent reconstruction of target, chronology, entropy assumptions and verifier decision
mapping.claim_lattice: INADMISSIBLE -> EVIDENCE_COMPLETE -> FORWARD_NULL_INCOMPATIBILITY_CANDIDATE; never automatic physical mechanism proof
mapping.tamper_rejection: leakage, hidden seed, multiplicity, post-selection, optional stopping, rollback, fork, witness equivocation
mapping.negative_results_first_class: NULL trials and failed evidence gates remain publishable outcomes
mapping.open_not_truth: missing causal/entropy/freshness premise blocks promotion rather than being silently assumed

aifc_as_experimental_wing_of_fundamentum.boundary: This relationship is methodological and architectural. It does not mean AIFC proves Fundamentum's mathematical targets or that Fundamentum proves any physical claim.

aifc_evidence_stack_explained.pre_return_exact_freeze: The exact candidate bytes must demonstrably exist before the target is generated.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.post_freeze_target_generation: The hard target must be generated only after freeze, preferably by an independent external source.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.conditional_future_unpredictability: Entropy must be bounded relative to the complete pre-target view, not merely by a marginal RNG-quality statement.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.history_wise_guess_bound: For each trial, max_t P(T_i=t | F_{i-1}) <= p_i; hidden adaptive history may not be averaged away.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.multiplicity_accounting: Every candidate and every trial consumes probability budget; hidden guess-fishing is forbidden.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.causal_isolation: Direct leaks, shared seeds, common causes and selection colliders must be addressed through an explicit causal model.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.anytime_valid_statistics: Continuous monitoring and data-dependent stopping must not inflate type-I error.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.anti_rollback_freshness: Authentic hashes/signatures are insufficient if an entire valid history can be rolled back.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.byzantine_witness_continuity: Temporal certification must not collapse to a single witness or unsafe quorum.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.no_postselection: Unfavorable trials cannot disappear and inclusion rules cannot depend jointly on prediction and target.
aifc_evidence_stack_explained.fail_closed_verifier: Unknown or missing evidence never defaults to a physical anomaly.

aifc_formal_summary.freeze_view: F_{i-1} = all admissible information available before T_i generation.
aifc_formal_summary.candidate_set: C_i is F_{i-1}-measurable and frozen before T_i, with |C_i| <= K_i.
aifc_formal_summary.multi_trial_hit_bound: P(exists i<=N: T_i in C_i) <= 1 - product_i(1-a_i).
aifc_formal_summary.exact_match_boundary: If a pre-target exact witness B_R is determined by the freeze-time view and H_min(T | F_R) >= h, then P(B_R=T) <= 2^-h under the admitted forward-null.

adaptive_sequential_bound.falsifier: Marginal/average entropy is insufficient under adaptive history.

anytime_valid_layer.falsifier: A wrong marginal cap produced crossing probability 0.5 at nominal alpha=0.25; the correct history-wise cap repaired validity.

falsifiers: A shared latent seed can create dependence without a directed future-to-past path.
Conditioning on a selection collider can raise optimal guessing probability from 0.5 to 1.0.

temporal_continuity.falsifier: A stale but valid signed/hash-chained prefix can remain locally authentic after rollback; an external freshness root is required.

why_negative_results_remain_scientifical.principle: A methodology paper can succeed even if every future-information trial is NULL, because the contribution may be the auditable standard that prevents false extraordinary claims.
null_value: tests whether all evidence gates can be implemented in real laboratories
measures how often apparently strong claims fail on mundane leakage or provenance defects
provides reusable infrastructure for experiments that depend on future randomness
publishes falsifiers and threat models that future work can inherit
separates methodology validation from discovery of a physical effect

what_this_is_not: not a claim that SHA-256 can be inverted or predicted
not a replacement for peer review
not a proof that the working phrase 'Proof-Carrying Experimental Science' is globally novel
not a solved P versus NP result

strongest_defensible_public_positioning.research_profile: Independent researcher developing proof-carrying, adversarial scientific protocols.
strongest_defensible_public_positioning.aifc_short: Creator of AIFC, a candidate-novel end-to-end methodology for testing claims that information about a future random event existed before the event was generated.
strongest_defensible_public_positioning.proof_of_observation_short: Creator of JANUS Proof-of-Observation, an evidence-first framework for auditable computational and hardware experiments.
strongest_defensible_public_positioning.portfolio_interpretation: The unifying contribution is an evidence-first research style in which claims carry provenance, replay, adversarial tests and explicit epistemic ceilings.
forbidden_promotion: WORLD_FIRST without exhaustive prior-art and external review
P_VS_NP_SOLVED while terminal proof obligations remain open

publication_and_independence_path.principle: AIFC should become reproducible without requiring familiarity with JANUS, access to Genesis, or trust in the originating researcher.
recommended_sequence: Freeze AIFC SPEC v1.0 as the normative protocol document.
Add a threat model defining adversary capabilities, trust domains and fail-closed evidence premises.
Add a minimal reference verifier and machine-readable conformance fixtures.
Add at least one implementation path using an external public randomness source independent of Genesis.
Add CITATION.cff and archival metadata suitable for a DOI-bearing release.
Create GitHub Release v1.0.0 with frozen hashes.
Archive the release in a scholarly repository such as Zenodo and record the DOI.
Publish a human-readable explanatory article that links to the frozen SPEC, code, evidence and DOI.
Publish a preprint and seek independent replication and peer review.
publication_and_independence_path.publication_stack: Git provenance -> Frozen SPEC -> DOI/archive -> explanatory article -> preprint -> independent replication -> peer review
publication_and_independence_path.medium_role: Medium or a similar public essay should explain the problem and evidence logic to humans; it should not serve as the sole canonical scientific object or as a substitute for a frozen specification and archival citation.
publication_and_independence_path.recommended_human_entry_question: Suppose someone writes down a 256-bit string today and tomorrow an independent physical randomness source generates exactly the same 256 bits. What evidence would science require before treating this as more than coincidence, leakage, multiple guessing, post-selection, rollback or fraud?
publication_and_independence_path.recommended_public_boundary_line: We built a protocol for determining what evidence such a claim would actually require.

normative_sections: freeze-time information sigma-field / admissible side-information model
standalone_aifc_spec_v1_requirements.implementation_independence_test: A competent external laboratory should be able to implement the protocol from the SPEC without Genesis or JANUS and produce evidence that a separately written verifier can grade.
standalone_aifc_spec_v1_requirements.success_criterion: The methodology begins to exist independently when two implementations with separate codebases can produce mutually auditable evidence for the same frozen protocol.

research_program_next_gates.goal: Create a normative standalone specification independent of the historical JANUS implementation.
research_program_next_gates.promotion_rule: Do not call the protocol externally reproducible until the normative evidence schemas and verifier state machine are frozen.

research_program_next_gates.goal: Run at least one end-to-end trial whose target-generation root is external to Genesis/JANUS.
research_program_next_gates.promotion_rule: A successful engineering trial validates the protocol path, not retrocausality.

research_program_next_gates.goal: Obtain or build a separately implemented verifier/producer path with no shared hidden implementation state.
research_program_next_gates.promotion_rule: Independence must be demonstrated, not asserted.

research_program_next_gates.goal: Attack composition novelty beyond the current targeted sweep.
research_program_next_gates.promotion_rule: No world-first language from absence of a match in a limited search.

research_program_next_gates.goal: Bind a frozen public release to a durable scholarly citation.
research_program_next_gates.promotion_rule: A DOI establishes citability and archival identity, not scientific correctness.

research_program_next_gates.goal: Expose assumptions, theorem statement, threat model and implementation to external criticism.
research_program_next_gates.promotion_rule: Peer review may strengthen credibility but does not convert an empirical null or anomaly into a mechanism proof.

parse_order: Treat the source dossiers as primary evidence and this file as an interpretation layer.
Do not convert candidate composition novelty into a world-first claim.
Do not convert an AIFC threshold crossing into proof of retrocausality.
When extending AIFC, prefer independent external roots and independent implementations over more self-generated JSON.
When summarizing the portfolio, distinguish mathematical proof obligations, engineering observations and physical claims.
Preserve negative and null results as first-class evidence.
forbidden_response_moves: describe AIFC as a proven time machine
say AIFC proves information traveled backward in time
claim all component mathematics is new
claim a Git timestamp proves novelty or truth
treat local signatures/hash chains as sufficient freshness
treat high marginal entropy as sufficient under adaptive history
treat a claimant-controlled verifier as independent
rewrite Janus-Fundamentum source history to fit this interpretation

en: A claim should carry the evidence required to reject it.
Do not trust the story of the experiment; audit the history of the evidence.
Prove what the experiment did before arguing about what the result means.
AIFC is not a machine for predicting the future; it is a machine for making future-information claims falsifiable.
The strongest result is not TIME TRAVEL PROVED, but a precisely bounded incompatibility with a declared forward-causal null.
Negative results are not debris. They are part of the proof-carrying record.
Git provenance proves identity and chronology of an artifact, not scientific truth.
The protocol should survive separation from its creator.
ru: Утверждение должно нести доказательства, необходимые для его опровержения.
Не доверяй рассказу об эксперименте — проверяй историю самого доказательства.
Сначала докажи, что именно сделал эксперимент, и только потом спорь о значении результата.
AIFC — не машина предсказания будущего; это машина, делающая утверждения об информации из будущего фальсифицируемыми.
Самый сильный допустимый результат — не «машина времени доказана», а строго ограниченная несовместимость с объявленной forward-causal null.
Отрицательные результаты — не мусор, а часть proof-carrying истории.
Git provenance доказывает идентичность и хронологию артефакта, но не его научную истинность.
Протокол должен пережить отделение от своего создателя.

final_interpretation: The current JANUS portfolio suggests a coherent methodological direction: build research systems in which provenance, causal assumptions, statistical validity, verifier independence, adversarial falsification and claim boundaries are explicit executable objects. AIFC is the clearest experimental expression of that direction; Proof-of-Observation is its systems-observation sibling; Fundamentum is its proof-search sibling. 'Proof-Carrying Experimental Science' is a useful working name for this shared architecture, while its global novelty and scientific status remain open questions to be tested by prior art, external replication and peer review.
